From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Bottom line:** The Seller calls this a "fair and balanced package". It isn't. Three positions work together so that almost no claim would ever succeed:

1. General disclosure of the whole data room.
2. A Buyer-knowledge bar covering anything "discoverable".
3. Caps and time limits applied to all Claims, including title, fraud and indemnities.

Every known problem is in the data room, so together these would leave the Buyer with almost no recourse. At the same time, the Seller's own Disclosure Letter confirms that several items the Update calls "addressed" or "adequate" are in fact unresolved:

- **Bluefen:** no consent has been given.
- **Riverlark:** the facility has not been repaid and no discharge has been given.
- **Ironquay:** AUD 180,000 is unpaid and the IP has not been assigned.
- **Employee bonuses:** AUD 420,000 is missing from the funds flow.
- **DD-006:** the privacy incident has not been investigated or resolved.

The quantified known exposures alone come to about **AUD 4.13m**, against a proposed general cap of **AUD 4.8m**. That figure excludes the Bluefen revenue at risk, the privacy incident and on-costs.

*Caveat: I have reviewed only the Seller's summary and Disclosure Letter, not the full SPA draft or the underlying DD documents (DD-002 to DD-012). The points below should be checked against those documents and settled by the supervising lawyer.*

---

## Part A: Structural issues (the limitations regime)

### 1. Limitations applying to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5, and the 12.3/13 default rule)
**Departure:** The Seller wants caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to apply to every Claim unless the SPA expressly says otherwise. That would capture:
- fundamental warranties;
- tax;
- specific indemnities;
- leakage and price adjustment;
- breach of covenant; and
- arguably fraud.

**Push back:**
- **Flip the default.** Limitations should apply only to Warranty Claims (excluding Fundamental and Tax Warranties) unless the SPA expressly says otherwise.
- **Carve out completely:**
  - fraud, dishonesty or wilful concealment by the Seller, its officers, employees or advisers;
  - Fundamental Warranties;
  - the Tax indemnity;
  - specific indemnities;
  - leakage, price adjustment and debt or debt-like amounts;
  - breach of Completion obligations and restrictive covenants.
- **Exclusive remedy and non-reliance:** these must not exclude claims for fraud. Under NSW law, a party generally cannot contract out of liability for its own fraud. Statutory claims for misleading or deceptive conduct (ACL s 18) also cannot be fully excluded, although a non-reliance clause can weaken them as a matter of evidence. Insist on an express fraud carve-out anyway.

### 2. General disclosure of the data room and public registers (Schedule 7; DL 1.1–1.2)
**Departure:** "Every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to" in the data room is treated as disclosed, along with the Accounts, statutory registers and public records. This turns the warranties into "the data room is accurate" and shifts all diligence risk to the Buyer. The cut-off of 22 September 2026 is also now more than six weeks old.

**Push back:**
- Only **specific disclosures** in the Disclosure Letter should qualify the warranties. They must be fair and identify the matter, and its nature and scope, in enough detail for a reasonable buyer to assess it.
- Delete general disclosure of the data room. If some data-room disclosure must be conceded as a trade-off, limit it to documents expressly cross-referenced against a specific warranty.
- Disclosure must **never** qualify Fundamental Warranties, the Tax indemnity or specific indemnities.
- Delete public-register disclosure, or limit it to searches of the Company made on a stated date.
- Require an updated disclosure at Completion. New matters should give the Buyer a right to terminate or claim, not narrow the warranties.

### 3. Buyer knowledge bar (cl 8.3)
**Departure:** The proposed bar is extremely broad. It covers:
- knowledge of the Buyer **or its advisers**;
- matters merely **"discoverable"**; and
- the entire data room and public records.

Combined with point 2, this would defeat most claims. It would also defeat any claim on matters the Buyer has already identified, which is precisely why we need indemnities for them.

**Push back:**
- Replace it with a clause preserving claims regardless of Buyer knowledge: the Buyer's rights are not affected by any investigation by, or knowledge of, the Buyer or its advisers, actual, constructive or imputed.
- At most, accept a bar limited to matters **fairly disclosed** in the Disclosure Letter, and only for general Warranty Claims.

### 4. Fundamental (title and capacity) warranties under the general cap and 18-month limit
**Departure:** The Seller says this is for "administrative simplicity". In substance it caps liability for failing to deliver the very shares being bought at 20% of the price. That is not market practice.

**Push back:**
- Cap Fundamental Warranties at **100% of the Purchase Price**.
- No de minimis or basket.
- Time limit of at least 6 years. Consider 7 years, or align with the 12-year limitation period if the SPA is executed as a deed.
- Fundamental Warranties should cover:
  - title;
  - capacity and authority;
  - no Encumbrances over the shares;
  - the issued share capital is complete, with no options, convertibles or rights to issue; and
  - solvency.

### 5. Cap, thresholds and time limits for general warranties (cl 12.1–12.3)
- **Cap of 20% (AUD 4.8m):** this is at the low end. Counter at 50%, with a possible landing at 30–40%. If W&I insurance is being considered, the Seller cap structure changes. Even so, insurers will exclude the known matters below, so specific Seller indemnities are needed regardless.
- **De minimis of AUD 25k:** propose AUD 10k. Related or similar claims arising from the same facts must be aggregated for de minimis purposes.
- **Basket of AUD 250k, excess only:** convert it to a **tipping basket**, so that once the threshold is reached the Buyer recovers from the first dollar. Propose 0.5% (AUD 120k).
- **18 months:** propose 24 months for general warranties. This gives at least two audit cycles to surface problems.
- **Tax:** the Tax Warranties and indemnity need their own regime. Use a time limit of at least the relevant ATO and Revenue NSW amendment periods plus a buffer (commonly 5–7 years), with no limit for fraud or evasion. They should not be subject to the general cap, basket or disclosure.
- **IP:** treat IP title warranties as quasi-fundamental. Use a higher cap and a longer period, particularly given Ironquay (see item 9).

---

## Part B: Specific diligence matters

### 6. Bluefen change-control consent (cl 3 / 6.3; DD-002; DL item 2)
**Risk:** Bluefen generates about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue, roughly 30% of the business. The Update says the consent is "addressed". The Disclosure Letter says no final consent exists and the cl 11.3 conditions have not been shown to be satisfied. A "reasonable endeavours" obligation, with the condition "treated as satisfied" on delivery of any written consent, would let the Seller deliver a **conditional or qualified** consent and force Completion.

**Push back:**
- Make it a **Condition Precedent for the Buyer's benefit only**, waivable only by the Buyer.
- The condition should be satisfied only by an **unconditional** written consent, in a form reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer, with evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are met. The consent must not change pricing, term or termination rights.
- Upgrade the Seller's obligation to **best or all reasonable endeavours**, with Buyer involvement in communications with Bluefen.
- Include a long-stop date and a Buyer termination right.
- Add a warranty that the Company has received no notice of termination or non-renewal and is not aware of any intention to give one.
- Consider a price adjustment or earn-out mechanism if Bluefen is lost or renegotiated within 12 months.

### 7. Riverlark Bank facility, about AUD 3.2m (cl 2 / 7; DD-003; DL item 3)
**Risk:** The deal is debt-free/cash-free, yet the Seller proposes a release **"following Completion"**. Two specific concerns:
- The change-control clause (cl 8.1) may mean Completion itself triggers default or acceleration.
- The security may extend over the Company's assets and possibly the shares. A post-Completion release leaves the Buyer owning a company with live, defaulted, secured debt.

**Push back:**
- The facility must be **repaid at Completion from the Purchase Price**, shown as a line item in the funds flow paid directly to Riverlark.
- Riverlark must deliver at Completion:
  - an executed payout letter;
  - a deed of release covering all security, guarantees and any share mortgage; and
  - PPSR financing-change statements, or an undertaking to lodge them within 1 business day.
- The release must be a **Condition or Completion deliverable**, not a post-Completion promise.
- All facility amounts, including break costs, accrued interest and fees, are Indebtedness and deducted from the price.
- Add an uncapped indemnity for any amount owing to Riverlark.

### 8. Employee Completion bonuses of AUD 420k plus on-costs (DD-005; DL item 5)
**Risk:** The Update says these are "a matter for the Seller" but leaves them out of the funds flow. If the Company pays them after Completion, the Buyer bears them. On top of the AUD 420k, the Company may owe:
- PAYG withholding;
- NSW payroll tax;
- possibly superannuation guarantee, depending on how the bonus is characterised; and
- workers compensation on-costs.

**Push back:**
- Treat the bonuses and all associated taxes and on-costs as **Transaction Costs / Debt-like Items**, deducted from the price and paid through payroll at or immediately after Completion. The Seller funds them via the funds flow.
- Add an uncapped specific indemnity for any amount above what is deducted.
- Require a full schedule: recipients, amounts, conditions, and whether any amounts are payable even if an employee later leaves.
- Add a warranty that no other change-of-control, retention or transaction payments exist.

### 9. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DD-004, DD-010; DL item 4)
**Risk:** Under cl 7.3 of DD-004, title to the SOW3 Project Materials passes **only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee**. DD-010 shows AUD 180k open. There is no evidence of payment and no confirmatory assignment. The Company may therefore not own IP it uses. An indemnity limited to "the specific SOW3 payment" does not cover:
- third-party infringement claims;
- injunctions;
- redevelopment or replacement costs; or
- loss of use.

**Push back:**
- **Condition or Completion deliverable:** payment of all SOW3 fees, either before Completion and treated as leakage, or as a funds-flow deduction. Ironquay must then deliver an executed **confirmatory assignment** of all Project Materials and a moral-rights consent.
- **Broad specific indemnity** for all Loss arising from the Company not owning, or not being entitled to use, the SOW3 materials. It should be outside the cap, basket, disclosure and knowledge limitations, and last at least 6 years.
- Verify any payment against bank records, not the ledger alone. The Disclosure Letter itself flags this gap.

### 10. DD-006 export and privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6; DL item 6)
**Risk:** About 1,240 records containing personal information were sent to an unintended external address. The Seller calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material". Relevant points:
- Given revenue of roughly AUD 12m (implied by Bluefen at 30%), the Company is likely an APP entity under the *Privacy Act 1988* (Cth).
- The Notifiable Data Breaches scheme requires an assessment within **30 days** of becoming aware of a suspected eligible breach.
- The incident was known by at least 22 September 2026, so that window may already have closed with no assessment shown.
- Exposure includes regulatory action (the civil penalty regime has been significantly strengthened), customer claims (including from Bluefen), and remediation costs.

**Push back:**
- Pre-Completion covenant requiring the Company to complete a documented NDB assessment, with external forensic support if appropriate, and make any required OAIC and individual notifications, with Buyer consultation.
- Specific indemnity for all Loss arising from DD-006, including regulatory penalties to the extent lawfully indemnifiable, investigation costs, notification and remediation, third-party and customer claims. It should be outside the cap, basket, disclosure and knowledge bar.
- Add a specific privacy and cyber warranty covering compliance, no other incidents, and no regulator correspondence.
- Consider a retention or escrow amount sized to the exposure.

### 11. Sandbar supplier renewals, 3 × AUD 110k = AUD 330k (DD-008, DD-011; DL item 8)
**Risk:** Three "related" renewals of identical value, which the Disclosure Letter says should be "read together for timing/scope". This pattern suggests a single commitment split to stay under a threshold, such as a material-contract definition, a conduct-of-business consent limit, or a board approval limit. The Seller calls them "ordinary course" but the Disclosure Letter does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.

**Push back:**
- Ask for the renewal documents, timing, approvals and business rationale. Confirm whether Sandbar is a related party of Harbourglass.
- Make sure the conduct-of-business and material-contract thresholds **aggregate related contracts**.
- If the renewals were entered into or prepaid after the locked-box or accounts date, or are not on arm's-length terms, treat them as leakage or require termination at the Seller's cost. Otherwise, require Buyer consent to any further renewals.

### 12. Title evidence (DD-012; DL item 10)
**Risk:** The register alone is not adequate evidence of title. The Disclosure Letter itself notes the Buyer has not verified it. There may also be Riverlark security over the shares.

**Push back:**
- Obtain current ASIC and PPSR searches against the Company and against Harbourglass as grantor.
- Require at Completion:
  - original share certificates, or a lost-certificate indemnity;
  - executed share transfer forms; and
  - releases of any share security.
- Back all of this with the uncapped Fundamental Warranties (item 4).

### 13. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"
Reject. See items 5 and 9. Tax requires a stand-alone indemnity covering pre-Completion periods, including payroll tax on the bonuses. IP title warrants a higher cap and longer period.

### 14. Lower-priority items: Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
The Seller says only that these documents "do not state" consent is required. That is not assurance. Steps:
- Review the documents for change-of-control triggers, including deemed-assignment wording.
- Make the landlord notification a Completion deliverable.
- Add a warranty that no consent is required and that no change of control gives any counterparty a termination right.

---

## Part C: Additional protections to propose

- **Retention or escrow:** Harbourglass is a fund vehicle that may distribute sale proceeds. Propose an escrow (for example 10–15% of the price, or amounts tied to specific exposures such as DD-006, Ironquay and Bluefen) or a creditworthy parent guarantee.
- **Bring-down:** warranties repeated at Completion, with a Buyer termination right for material breach or MAC, and a disclosure-update mechanism that does not cure breaches.
- **W&I:** if pursued, the known matters (items 6–11) will be excluded by the insurer. The Seller indemnities above remain essential.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Buyer response | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Scope of limitations | Apply to all Claims | Apply only to general Warranty Claims; carve out fraud, fundamentals, tax, indemnities, leakage, covenants | **Critical** |
| 2 | General disclosure | Whole data room plus public records | Specific, fair disclosure only; never against fundamentals, tax or indemnities | **Critical** |
| 3 | Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Advisers' knowledge and anything "discoverable" bars claims | Buyer claims preserved regardless of knowledge | **Critical** |
| 4 | Title and capacity | 20% cap, 18 months | 100% cap, at least 6–7 years, no thresholds | **Critical** |
| 5 | Riverlark AUD 3.2m | Release after Completion | Repay from price at Completion; payout letter, deed of release, PPSR releases as deliverables | **Critical** |
| 6 | Bluefen (30% revenue) | Reasonable endeavours; any written consent suffices | Buyer-only CP; unconditional consent; cl 11.3 conditions evidenced; long-stop and termination right | **Critical** |
| 7 | Ironquay IP | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment | Payment plus confirmatory assignment as CP; broad uncapped IP indemnity | High |
| 8 | DD-006 privacy incident | "Not expected to be material" | Pre-Completion NDB assessment; specific uncapped indemnity; escrow | High |
| 9 | Bonuses AUD 420k plus on-costs | Outside funds flow | Debt-like item deducted from price; indemnity | High |
| 10 | Tax | General regime | Stand-alone tax indemnity, outside cap, longer period | High |
| 11 | General cap and thresholds | 20%; AUD 25k; AUD 250k deductible; 18 months | 30–50%; AUD 10k with aggregation; tipping basket at about AUD 120k; 24 months | Medium |
| 12 | Sandbar AUD 330k | Ordinary course | Request documents; aggregate thresholds; leakage or consent treatment | Medium |
| 13 | Title evidence | Register only | ASIC and PPSR searches, certificates, transfers, share-security release | Medium |
| 14 | Lease and Mossvale | No consent "stated" | Verify; notification as deliverable; no-trigger warranty | Low |
| 15 | Credit support | None | Escrow or parent guarantee | High |

**Suggested next steps:**
1. Obtain and review the full SPA draft and DD-002 to DD-012, particularly Bluefen cl 11.2–11.3, Riverlark cl 8.1/9.2, Ironquay cl 7.3, and the DD-006 incident file.
2. Ask for an updated Disclosure Letter, since the 22 September cut-off is stale.
3. Prepare the mark-up with Part A as non-negotiable principles. Specific indemnities and the funds-flow corrections should go in alongside the Bluefen and Riverlark Conditions.
4. Consider giving ground on the general cap and time limits in exchange for the critical items.

The Disclosure Letter says no final consent exists and the cl 11.3 conditions have not been shown to be satisfied. A "reasonable endeavours" obligation, with the condition "treated as satisfied" on delivery of any written consent, would let the Seller deliver a **conditional or qualified** consent and force Completion.

**Push back:**
- Make it a **Condition Precedent for the Buyer's benefit only**, waivable only by the Buyer.
- The condition should be satisfied only by an **unconditional** written consent, in a form reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer, with evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are met. The consent must not change pricing, term or termination rights.
- Upgrade the Seller's obligation to **best or all reasonable endeavours**, with Buyer involvement in communications with Bluefen.
- Include a long-stop date and a Buyer termination right.
- Add a warranty that the Company has received no notice of termination or non-renewal and is not aware of any intention to give one.
- Consider a price adjustment or earn-out mechanism if Bluefen is lost or renegotiated within 12 months.

### 7. Riverlark Bank facility, about AUD 3.2m (cl 2 / 7; DD-003; DL item 3)
**Risk:** The deal is debt-free/cash-free, yet the Seller proposes a release **"following Completion"**. Two specific concerns:
- The change-control clause (cl 8.1) may mean Completion itself triggers default or acceleration.
- The security may extend over the Company's assets and possibly the shares. A post-Completion release leaves the Buyer owning a company with live, defaulted, secured debt.

**Push back:**
- The facility must be **repaid at Completion from the Purchase Price**, shown as a line item in the funds flow paid directly to Riverlark.
- Riverlark must deliver at Completion:
  - an executed payout letter;
  - a deed of release covering all security, guarantees and any share mortgage; and
  - PPSR financing-change statements, or an undertaking to lodge them within 1 business day.
- The release must be a **Condition or Completion deliverable**, not a post-Completion promise.
- All facility amounts, including break costs, accrued interest and fees, are Indebtedness and deducted from the price.
- Add an uncapped indemnity for any amount owing to Riverlark.

### 8. Employee Completion bonuses of AUD 420k plus on-costs (DD-005; DL item 5)
**Risk:** The Update says these are "a matter for the Seller" but leaves them out of the funds flow. If the Company pays them after Completion, the Buyer bears them. On top of the AUD 420k, the Company may owe:
- PAYG withholding;
- NSW payroll tax;
- possibly superannuation guarantee, depending on how the bonus is characterised; and
- workers compensation on-costs.

**Push back:**
- Treat the bonuses and all associated taxes and on-costs as **Transaction Costs / Debt-like Items**, deducted from the price and paid through payroll at or immediately after Completion. The Seller funds them via the funds flow.
- Add an uncapped specific indemnity for any amount above what is deducted.
- Require a full schedule: recipients, amounts, conditions, and whether any amounts are payable even if an employee later leaves.
- Add a warranty that no other change-of-control, retention or transaction payments exist.

### 9. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DD-004, DD-010; DL item 4)
**Risk:** Under cl 7.3 of DD-004, title to the SOW3 Project Materials passes **only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee**. DD-010 shows AUD 180k open. There is no evidence of payment and no confirmatory assignment. The Company may therefore not own IP it uses. An indemnity limited to "the specific SOW3 payment" does not cover:
- third-party infringement claims;
- injunctions;
- redevelopment or replacement costs; or
- loss of use.

**Push back:**
- **Condition or Completion deliverable:** payment of all SOW3 fees, either before Completion and treated as leakage, or as a funds-flow deduction. Ironquay must then deliver an executed **confirmatory assignment** of all Project Materials and a moral-rights consent.
- **Broad specific indemnity** for all Loss arising from the Company not owning, or not being entitled to use, the SOW3 materials. It should be outside the cap, basket, disclosure and knowledge limitations, and last at least 6 years.
- Verify any payment against bank records, not the ledger alone. The Disclosure Letter itself flags this gap.

### 10. DD-006 export and privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6; DL item 6)
**Risk:** About 1,240 records containing personal information were sent to an unintended external address. The Seller calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material". Relevant points:
- Given revenue of roughly AUD 12m (implied by Bluefen at 30%), the Company is likely an APP entity under the *Privacy Act 1988* (Cth).
- The Notifiable Data Breaches scheme requires an assessment within **30 days** of becoming aware of a suspected eligible breach.
- The incident was known by at least 22 September 2026, so that window may already have closed with no assessment shown.
- Exposure includes regulatory action (the civil penalty regime has been significantly strengthened), customer claims (including from Bluefen), and remediation costs.

**Push back:**
- Pre-Completion covenant requiring the Company to complete a documented NDB assessment, with external forensic support if appropriate, and make any required OAIC and individual notifications, with Buyer consultation.
- Specific indemnity for all Loss arising from DD-006, including regulatory penalties to the extent lawfully indemnifiable, investigation costs, notification and remediation, third-party and customer claims. It should be outside the cap, basket, disclosure and knowledge bar.
- Add a specific privacy and cyber warranty covering compliance, no other incidents, and no regulator correspondence.
- Consider a retention or escrow amount sized to the exposure.

### 11. Sandbar supplier renewals, 3 × AUD 110k = AUD 330k (DD-008, DD-011; DL item 8)
**Risk:** Three "related" renewals of identical value, which the Disclosure Letter says should be "read together for timing/scope". This pattern suggests a single commitment split to stay under a threshold, such as a material-contract definition, a conduct-of-business consent limit, or a board approval limit. The Seller calls them "ordinary course" but the Disclosure Letter does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.

**Push back:**
- Ask for the renewal documents, timing, approvals and business rationale. Confirm whether Sandbar is a related party of Harbourglass.
- Make sure the conduct-of-business and material-contract thresholds **aggregate related contracts**.
- If the renewals were entered into or prepaid after the locked-box or accounts date, or are not on arm's-length terms, treat them as leakage or require termination at the Seller's cost. Otherwise, require Buyer consent to any further renewals.

### 12. Title evidence (DD-012; DL item 10)
**Risk:** The register alone is not adequate evidence of title. The Disclosure Letter itself notes the Buyer has not verified it. There may also be Riverlark security over the shares.

**Push back:**
- Obtain current ASIC and PPSR searches against the Company and against Harbourglass as grantor.
- Require at Completion:
  - original share certificates, or a lost-certificate indemnity;
  - executed share transfer forms; and
  - releases of any share security.
- Back all of this with the uncapped Fundamental Warranties (item 4).

### 13. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"
Reject. See items 5 and 9. Tax requires a stand-alone indemnity covering pre-Completion periods, including payroll tax on the bonuses. IP title warrants a higher cap and longer period.

### 14. Lower-priority items: Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
The Seller says only that these documents "do not state" consent is required. That is not assurance. Steps:
- Review the documents for change-of-control triggers, including deemed-assignment wording.
- Make the landlord notification a Completion deliverable.
- Add a warranty that no consent is required and that no change of control gives any counterparty a termination right.

## Part C: Additional protections to propose

- **Retention or escrow:** Harbourglass is a fund vehicle that may distribute sale proceeds. Propose an escrow (for example 10–15% of the price, or amounts tied to specific exposures such as DD-006, Ironquay and Bluefen) or a creditworthy parent guarantee.
- **Bring-down:** warranties repeated at Completion, with a Buyer termination right for material breach or MAC, and a disclosure-update mechanism that does not cure breaches.
- **W&I:** if pursued, the known matters (items 6–11) will be excluded by the insurer. The Seller indemnities above remain essential.
